comments.body:
DECISION (AC1): DEPRECATE, not remove. Recorded with the evidence that decided it.

WHY NOT OPTION 2 (remove now). Option 2's premise — that the key never changed behaviour in any shipped release where the port was already dormant — is FALSE. At shipped tag v0.10.1 the inbound probe was fully reachable (reconcile.py, apply_inbound.py, inbound_probe.py present and wired) and adapters/jira/probe.py::_resolve_resolved_statuses read jira.resolved_statuses to classify. The key was live and behaviour-affecting in a shipped release; it only became inert by v0.11.0 (the current version, released 2026-08-07), by which point bug 3b5f had already removed the consumers. On top of that, the pre-f020 docs actively told operators to set it: "Set it if your self-hosted workflow names its resolved states differently — otherwise a resolved issue is misclassified." So real pyproject.toml files plausibly carry this key, and hard-removing it is a genuine upgrade hazard.

WHY NOT OPTION 3 (keep for a future reader). ADR 0028 rules absence-vs-deletion discrimination OUTBOUND-owned, and the outbound path (outbound_differ._safe_get_issue + binding_walk) discriminates on HTTP status, not workflow status names. No concrete future consumer exists.

WHY NOT HARD REMOVAL WITH A TOMBSTONE, i.e. the code_health.enabled precedent. That precedent (delete the field, add a warn-class tombstone so existing config still loads with a warning) is the right END state and is exactly what the follow-up ticket specifies. But it was applied "per the operator ruling" on bug a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1 — sign-off came first. There is no such ruling here, and removing a documented operator-facing key is user-visible, so this ticket does the conservative half and defers the removal to an operator decision.

WHAT WAS EXECUTED (AC2-AC4):
- Both keys registered as _scheduled cfg retirements in _deprecations.py (replacement "", remove_in v1.0.0). They still parse and validate byte-identically; the only new behaviour is a warning.
- coerce_sparse warns via a new _warn_deprecated_keys helper that looks the key up in _deprecations.REGISTRY directly. This adopts the plan-review's advisory finding (do not maintain a second parallel table). Extracting the helper also kept coerce_sparse under the C901 ceiling, which the inline loop had pushed from 15 to 16 — baselining that debt would have been the wrong trade.
- _message now words an empty-replacement scheduled entry as a retirement ("no longer has any effect") rather than "use <blank>", mirroring the branch _tombstone_message already had.
- The write-only DC plumbing is GONE: _TransportBase's resolved_statuses param and _resolved_statuses attribute, JiraDataCenterSettings.resolved_statuses, its resolution, DEFAULT_RESOLVED_STATUSES, and backend.py's ctor kwarg. Nothing read the value, so this is behaviour-neutral.
- Because that removed the last read of ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses, BOTH schema fields now carry a `# read-via:` marker pointing at the follow-up f408-64ad-ee41-46b6; the heldout marker test now pins exactly two markers naming that ticket.
- docs/config.md and docs/user-guide.md both describe the keys as deprecated, warning, scheduled for v1.0.0, removal tracked on f408. This also fixes the pre-existing inconsistency where user-guide.md attributed the f020/inert story to the reconciler key while the schema and config.md attributed it to the jira key.

RECOMMENDATION carried to f408-64ad-ee41-46b6 (created, linked discovered_from): remove both keys via warn-class tombstones following the code_health.enabled precedent, once an operator signs off. Warn-class rather than error-class because neither key is operationally load-bearing — nothing breaks if it is ignored.

  56 passed in 18.47s

  $ python -m pytest tests/unit tests/scripts -q     # full sweep
  6283 passed, 11 skipped

NOTE ON THE MODULE-SIZE GATE, recorded because it changed the design. The full sweep initially
FAILED test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap: _config_schema.py was already at 798 LOC against
the 800 hard cap, and the new warning helper pushed it to 824. Rather than baseline or shave
comments, the helper moved to `_deprecations.py` as `warn_deprecated_cfg_keys` — the correct
call-graph seam, since it is registry logic and `_config_schema` already imports from
`_deprecations` (no cycle). `_config_schema.py` is back to 798 LOC, i.e. this change is
size-neutral on that file, and `_deprecations.py` sits at 419.

Two other findings folded in during implementation:
* The plan-review's advisory A1 finding was ADOPTED — no parallel table of deprecated keys;
  the registry is consulted directly.
* Extracting the helper also resolved a C901 regression (coerce_sparse 15 -> 16), so the
  complexity baseline shows new=0 rather than absorbing new debt.

# The `resolved_statuses` config keys have no reader after f020

Task [rebar:f020-0960-2c42-4d61] deleted the dormant inbound absence-probe port, including
`classify_probe_response` — the only reader of the operator-facing resolved-status config. The
keys still validate; nothing consults them.

## DECISION: deprecate (option 1), do NOT remove now

Recorded with its reason, per AC1. Evidence gathered before deciding:

1. **Option 2's premise is false.** "Remove now" rests on the key never having changed
   behaviour in a shipped release where the port was already dormant. At tag **v0.10.1** the
   inbound probe was fully reachable (`reconcile.py`, `apply_inbound.py`, `inbound_probe.py`)
   and `adapters/jira/probe.py::_resolve_resolved_statuses` read `jira.resolved_statuses` to
   classify. The key WAS live and behaviour-affecting in a shipped release. It became inert
   only by v0.11.0 (current version).
2. **Operators were told to set it.** The pre-f020 `docs/config.md` row read: "Set it if your
   self-hosted workflow names its resolved states differently — otherwise a resolved issue is
   misclassified." Real `pyproject.toml`s plausibly carry the key.
3. **Option 3 is dead.** ADR 0028 rules absence-vs-deletion discrimination OUTBOUND-owned; the
   outbound path (`outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` + `binding_walk`) discriminates on HTTP
   status, not workflow names, so no concrete future reader exists.

So a user-visible surface with a real behavioural past is being retired. The project's own
precedent for this shape (`code_health.enabled`, `reconciler.lock_backend`) was applied "per
the operator ruling" — i.e. hard removal got operator sign-off first. Absent that sign-off
here, this ticket does the conservative half: keep the keys ACCEPTED and VALIDATED, warn on
use naming the removal release, remove only the internal non-operator-facing plumbing, and
file the hard removal as a follow-up requiring operator sign-off.

## Current state (verified line numbers)

* `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:459-465` — `ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses`.
* `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:484-490` — `JiraConfig.resolved_statuses`; line 489 is the
  `# read-via: inert pending task 549c-...` marker parked by f020.
* `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:697` / `:707` — the two `_as_str_list` coercers.
* DC chain, all write-only: `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:33-36`
  (`DEFAULT_RESOLVED_STATUSES`), `:48` (NamedTuple field), `:101-105` (the ONLY read of
  `ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses`), `:122`; `backend.py:303` (ctor kwarg);
  `_base.py:98,105,113-119` (`_resolved_statuses` param + attribute). Nothing consults the
  stored value — grep for `_resolved_statuses` finds only docstrings, the annotation, the
  assignment, and one test assertion.
* Docs: `docs/config.md:277-282` (jira key), `docs/user-guide.md:498` (reconciler key).
* Gate: `scripts/check_config_reads.py`; `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py:316-330`
  pins EXACTLY ONE ticket-pointing marker naming `resolved_statuses` + `549c-032f-6cb0-4258`.

## Plan

1. **File the follow-up removal ticket** (hard removal + tombstone, needs operator sign-off);
   `link <new> 549c-032f-6cb0-4258 discovered_from`. Its id is the new marker pointer.
2. **`src/rebar/_deprecations.py`** — add two `_scheduled("cfg", ...)` rows for
   `jira.resolved_statuses` and `reconciler.resolved_statuses`, replacement `""`,
   `remove_in=_MAJOR`. Extend `_message` to handle an empty replacement, mirroring the wording
   `_tombstone_message` already uses for that case, so the message reads as a retirement rather
   than "use <blank>".
3. **`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`** — add a small section→keys table of deprecated-but-honored
   keys and, in `coerce_sparse`, emit `warn_deprecated(f"cfg:{sect}.{key}")` when such a key is
   present. Coercion/validation is UNCHANGED, so existing config keeps loading identically; the
   only new behaviour is the warning.
4. **Remove the write-only DC plumbing** (AC4): the `_base.py` ctor param, annotation and
   assignment; the `backend.py:303` kwarg; the `settings.py` NamedTuple field, its resolution
   and `DEFAULT_RESOLVED_STATUSES`. Behaviour-neutral — nothing read the value.
5. **`# read-via:` markers** — step 4 removes the last read of `ReconcilerConfig`'s field, so
   both fields now need a marker. Re-point the existing one (line 489) and add one for the
   reconciler field, both naming the step-1 ticket. Update
   `test_check_config_reads_heldout.py:316-330` to expect TWO markers naming the new ticket.
6. **Docs** — `docs/config.md` and `docs/user-guide.md` re-describe both keys as DEPRECATED
   (accepted, validated, inert, warns, scheduled for removal in v1.0.0, removal tracked on the
   step-1 ticket). Also fixes the existing inconsistency where user-guide.md:498 attributes the
   f020/inert story to the reconciler key while the schema and config.md attribute it to jira.
7. **Tests** — update the DC settings/characterization tests that pin the removed constant and
   the transport attribute; add coverage that setting either key still loads AND warns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the decision and its reason are recorded on this ticket
- [x] both keys still load and validate unchanged, and emit a registered deprecation warning
      naming the removal release
- [x] the DC transport's `resolved_statuses` param / `_resolved_statuses` attribute is removed
- [x] `docs/config.md` and `docs/user-guide.md` match the decision for both keys
- [x] the config-read gate passes and its heldout marker test matches the new marker set
- [x] the follow-up hard-removal ticket exists, is linked, and is named by the markers/docs
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` green; change `Verified +1` before close [operator-attested]
